items.title: Why Objective Chance Challenges Theistic Evolution | Alex Rosenberg
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Can an omniscient God create a world governed by genuine chance?*

Alex Rosenberg argues that natural selection ultimately depends on objective chance and that this creates a conceptual problem for attempts to reconcile Darwinism with Christian theism.

0:00 Why Rosenberg Rejects Accommodationism
3:23 Darwinism Depends on Objective Chance
5:18 Why Omniscience Creates a Problem
7:50 Entropy, Chance, and the Limits of Reconciliation
10:12 The Problem for Reductionism and Theism

*Alexander Rosenberg* is an American philosopher and novelist. He is the R. Taylor Cole Professor of Philosophy at Duke University, well known for contributions to philosophy of biology and philosophy of economics. Rosenberg describes himself as a "naturalist".

items.title: Can All Major Religions Be Valid? | John Hick
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Could religions contradict one another and still be valid responses to the same transcendent reality?*

John Hick rejects both religious exclusivism and inclusivism, proposing instead that the world's major faiths are culturally different human responses to an ultimate reality that transcends any one religious description.

0:00 Why Do Religions Contradict Each Other?
0:51 Exclusivism, Inclusivism, and Pluralism
1:54 Why Hick Rejects Exclusivism and Inclusivism
2:56 Can Contradictory Ideas of God Be Reconciled?
4:03 What Experience Do Religions Share?
5:17 Is There a Fourth Alternative to Pluralism?
6:16 Would Religions Accept the Pluralistic Hypothesis?

*John Hick* (1922–2012) was a British philosopher of religion and theologian known for his influential work on religious pluralism. His research also made significant contributions to theodicy, eschatology, Christology, and the epistemology of religion.

items.title: Are God's Reasons Beyond Human Understanding? | Michael Tooley
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if the reason we cannot reconcile God with evil is simply that God's reasons are beyond human understanding?*

Michael Tooley examines skeptical theism, challenging the claim that unknown goods could defeat the probabilistic argument from evil and asking whether unknown evils must be given equal weight.

0:00 Can Skeptical Theism Undermine the Argument From Evil?
1:06 Could Unknown Evils Cancel Unknown Goods?
3:44 Can We Assign Probabilities to What We Cannot Know?

9:59 Is Skeptical Theism Circular?
11:54 Could an Afterlife Ultimately Justify All Suffering?

*Michael Tooley* is Emeritus Distinguished Professor of Philosophy at the University of Colorado Boulder. He received a Boulder Faculty Assembly Excellence in Research Award in 1998 for his book _Time, Tense, and Causation,_ and is the author of the new book _Causation: A Defense of a Non-Reductionist Approach_ (Oxford, 2026).

items.title: Did Morality Evolve Through Group Competition? | Rachell Powell
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:

Rachell Powell explores why inclusive fitness may not fully explain biological altruism and argues that group competition and social organization could help explain the emergence of ultra-cooperation, social norms, and morality-like systems in both humans and social insects.

Philosopher *Rachell Powell* explores how modern healthcare reshapes human evolution. By relaxing natural selection, medicine may be pushing humanity toward greater dependence on advanced technology—raising a striking paradox: to preserve human health as we know it, we may need to intervene more, not less.

items.title: Should We Choose a Theory of Consciousness? | Alex Gómez-Marín
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if every major theory of consciousness is partly right and partly wrong?*

Alex Gómez-Marín explains why he resists committing to materialism, dualism, idealism, or even panpsychism, arguing for intellectual flexibility while asking whether truth alone should guide our theories or whether goodness and beauty also reveal something about reality.

0:00 Why Stay Agnostic About Consciousness?
0:36 What Is Your Best Theory of Consciousness?
1:02 Are All Theories Partly Right and Partly Wrong?
2:07 Why Committing to One Theory Can Be Dangerous
2:49 Does Experience Transcend Theory?
4:30 Should Ethics Influence Theories of Reality?
6:08 Do Truth, Goodness, and Beauty Reveal Reality?

*Alex Gómez-Marín* is a Spanish physicist turned neuroscientist. He holds a PhD in theoretical physics and a Masters in biophysics from the University of Barcelona. He was a research fellow at the EMBL-CRG Centre for Genomic Regulation and at the Champalimaud Centre for the Unknown in Lisbon. His research spans from the origins of the arrow of time in inert systems, to the neurobiology of action-perception in living organisms such as flies, worms, mice, and humans.

items.title: Can Quantum Physics Solve the Binding Problem? | Mike Wiest
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*How does the brain combine separate neural processes into one unified conscious experience?*

Mike Wiest argues that the phenomenal binding problem poses a fundamental challenge for classical theories of consciousness and explores whether quantum entanglement could provide the unity conscious experience requires.

0:00 Macroscopic Quantum Effects
1:13 The Phenomenal Binding Problem
5:00 Quantum Entanglement and Binding
7:43 Quantum Consciousness and Panpsychism
9:42 Connecting Active Inference With Quantum Physics

*Michael C. Wiest* holds a Ph.D. from Michigan State University and is an Associate Professor of Neuroscience at Wellesley College, where he studies how the brain integrates sensory information to create conscious perception. His research contributes to a better understanding of disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, dyslexia, and ADHD.
